protocol.name: zxr_shell_v2

protocol.description:
This protocol allows clients to render three-dimensional content that the compositor composites, together with content from other clients, into one shared, depth-tested space presented on a head-mounted display.
A client renders its content from compositor-supplied view and projection matrices and submits, for every view, a colour image and a depth image as one atomic frame. The compositor resolves visibility between clients using the submitted depth. Geometry never crosses the wire; the compositor never re-renders client content, and clients never learn the composed result.
Coordinate conventions, used by every interface in this protocol: spaces are right-handed and metric, with y up and -z forward. Matrices are stored as arrays of 16 IEEE 754 binary32 values in native endianness, column-major, and act on column vectors (matrix times vector). A view matrix transforms positions from the local reference space into a view's eye space; a projection matrix transforms eye space into clip space with clip z over w in [0, 1]. Quaternions are unit Hamilton quaternions in x, y, z, w order describing active rotations composed by left multiplication. Image buffers use the core Wayland raster convention: the first pixel is the top-left corner, rows run top to bottom. All 64-bit protocol values split into _hi/_lo argument pairs combine as value = ((uint64)hi << 32) | lo.
This protocol continues the zxr_shell_unstable_v1 protocol of the wxrc compositor, which itself descended from the Motorcar research compositor. The per-view model, the surface role, and the typed colour/depth buffer distinction survive from version 1; the folded model-view-projection matrix event and the composite wl_buffer wrapper do not.
The key words "must", "must not", "required", "shall", "shall not", "should", "should not", "recommended", "may", and "optional" in this document are to be interpreted as described in IETF RFC 2119.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the experimental phase. Backward incompatible changes may be added without bumping the major version of the extension. As such, gating usage on the protocol's presence is discouraged outside Mura itself.

interface.name: zxr_shell_v2
interface.description:
The global entry point. It defines one protocol domain per bound shell object: the views, seats, surfaces, timing object, and frame ids used together must all originate from the same shell object. Passing an object from a different shell domain where a domain sibling is required raises the foreign_object error on the receiving object's interface.
On binding, the compositor sends the clock event, then the initial state batch: zero or more depth_format and transport events and one view event per composed view, terminated by done. Whenever the supported formats, transports, or view set change, the compositor sends the changed state followed by done; each batch atomically replaces the previous format and transport sets. This allows changes to the shell state to be seen as atomic, even if they happen via multiple events. Clients must not issue get_xr_surface or get_frame_timing before the first done event; such requests raise the not_ready error.

entry.name: role
entry.summary: given wl_surface already has another role

entry.name: surface_has_buffer
entry.summary: given wl_surface has a buffer attached or committed

entry.name: defunct_surfaces
entry.summary: shell destroyed before its child objects

entry.name: timing_exists
entry.summary: a frame timing object already exists for this shell

entry.name: not_ready
entry.summary: request sent before the initial state batch completed

enum.name: transport
enum.description: How image contents reach the compositor. Every compositor must accept shm; dmabuf is the intended production transport. The meaning of the submitted images is identical on every transport. Allocation ownership and further transports are deferred to a later revision of this protocol.

entry.name: shm
entry.summary: wl_shm buffers

entry.name: dmabuf
entry.summary: zwp_linux_dmabuf_v1 buffers with explicit sync

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the shell object. This request must be sent after destroying all objects created from it; otherwise the defunct_surfaces error is raised. Objects bound from other zxr_shell_v2 globals are not affected.

request.name: get_xr_surface
request.description:
Create a zxr_surface_v2 role object for the given surface, assigning the XR role. If the surface already has another role, or already has an XR role object, the role error is raised. If the surface has a buffer attached or committed at the time of this request, the surface_has_buffer error is raised.
The XR role is permanent: it remains assigned for the lifetime of the wl_surface. Attaching a wl_buffer to an XR surface with wl_surface.attach raises the zxr_surface_v2.buffer_forbidden error; image content is carried exclusively by frame slots.

request.name: get_frame_timing
request.description: Create the frame timing object for this shell's domain. At most one timing object may exist per shell object at a time; a second request while one exists raises the timing_exists error. Frame ids are scoped to the shell domain and are unique until retired; they are never reused within the lifetime of the shell object.

request.name: get_seat

description.summary: extend a seat with spatial input

request.description: Create a zxr_seat_v2 object extending the given wl_seat with spatial input capabilities.

event.name: clock
event.description: Tells the client in which clock domain the compositor interprets and produces every timestamp of this protocol domain — frame times, presentation feedback, and input events — as a POSIX clockid_t. Sent once, before the initial state batch. The clock does not change for the lifetime of the shell object, and all shell objects on one client connection use the same clock. The compositor should prefer a clock which does not jump and is not slewed.

event.name: depth_format
event.description: One supported depth image format, as a DRM FOURCC format code, valid on every advertised transport. Sent once per supported format within a state batch; the batch's formats atomically replace all previously advertised depth formats at the following done event. Colour formats are negotiated through the transport's own mechanism (wl_shm.format; zwp_linux_dmabuf_v1 default feedback for format and modifier eligibility, which applies to slot images exactly as it applies to attached buffers).

event.name: transport
event.description: One supported transport. Sent once per supported transport within a state batch; the batch's transports atomically replace the previous set at the following done event.

event.name: view
event.description: Announces a view belonging to this shell domain. Views announced and not yet finished form the domain's active view set; the set becomes effective at the following done event.

event.name: done

description.summary: the shell state batch is complete

event.description: Ends a state batch. The format and transport sets sent since the previous done event (or since bind) atomically replace the previous sets, and view set changes take effect. This allows changes to the shell state to be seen as atomic, even if they happen via multiple events.

interface.name: zxr_view_v2
interface.description:
A view is one perspective the compositor composes — typically one eye of a head-mounted display. Views are announced by zxr_shell_v2.view and belong to that shell's domain.
The view's slowly-changing properties arrive through events on this object, terminated by done; a property batch applies to frame snapshots that begin after its done event. Per-frame view and projection matrices never arrive here; they are part of the atomic frame snapshot on zxr_frame_timing_v2, so that matrices and images can never pair across frames.

request.name: destroy

event.name: resolution
event.description: The recommended pixel size for images rendered for this view. Both dimensions are always positive. A client may submit other sizes; the compositor samples the full image, scaling with at least bilinear filtering, at a quality cost.

event.name: fov
event.description: The field of view of this view, as the signed tangents of the four half-angles from the view's optical axis: tan_left and tan_down are negative or zero, tan_right and tan_up are positive or zero. Informational — clients may use it for culling and allocation heuristics; the authoritative projection arrives in each frame snapshot.

event.name: done

description.summary: the view property batch is complete

event.description: Ends a view property batch. Properties sent since the previous done event (or since the view event) apply to frame snapshots beginning after this event. This allows changes to the view properties to be seen as atomic, even if they happen via multiple events.

event.name: finished

description.summary: the view will no longer be composed

event.description:
Sent when the compositor removes the view. The compositor will immediately consider the object inert. Any requests will be ignored except the destroy request; there won't be any more events referencing this object.
The view leaves the active view set at the next zxr_shell_v2.done event. At that same point, every frame slot's attachments, sync points, and depth metadata for this view are discarded by the compositor: attached wl_buffers are released, and pending release points for this view's images are signalled when any outstanding compositor access completes. Slot requests naming the inert view object are ignored.

interface.name: zxr_seat_v2

description.summary: spatial input capabilities of a seat

interface.description: Spatial input state for one wl_seat. The capabilities event announces which spatial devices the seat offers; a batch of capability changes is terminated by done.

entry.name: ray
entry.summary: the seat has a pointing ray

entry.name: pointer_6dof
entry.summary: the seat has a tracked 6DoF pointer

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the spatial seat object. Ray and pointer objects created from it are not affected.

request.name: get_ray
request.description: Create a zxr_ray_v2 object for this seat. If the seat does not have the ray capability, the compositor ignores the request except for creating the object, which will never send events. Clients should hide or disable the UI elements that depend on absent capabilities.

request.name: get_pointer_6dof
request.description: Create a zxr_pointer_6dof_v2 object for this seat. If the seat does not have the pointer_6dof capability, the compositor ignores the request except for creating the object, which will never send events. Clients should hide or disable the UI elements that depend on absent capabilities.

event.name: capabilities
event.description: The spatial input capabilities of this seat. Sent on creation and whenever the capabilities change.

event.name: done
event.description: Ends a capability batch. This allows changes to the seat state to be seen as atomic, even if they happen via multiple events.

interface.name: zxr_surface_v2
interface.description:
The XR role object of a wl_surface. The surface's content is defined exclusively by submitted frame slots.
A surface is initially unmapped. It becomes mapped when a submission is composed for the first time, and unmapped again by the clear request. Destroying this object unmaps the surface and discards its XR state; the XR role itself remains assigned to the wl_surface (see zxr_shell_v2.get_xr_surface), so the wl_surface cannot take another role. If the wl_surface is destroyed first, this object becomes inert: any requests will be ignored except the destroy request, and there won't be any more events referencing this object.
The compositor assigns the surface a bounding volume through the configure event. The client must render its content inside the acknowledged bounds, in its own model space; the compositor enforces clipping regardless of client cooperation, against the most recently acknowledged bounds at each submission.

entry.name: buffer_forbidden
entry.summary: wl_surface.attach on an XR surface

entry.name: unconfigured
entry.summary: submit before the first ack_configure

entry.name: incomplete_slot
entry.summary: submitted slot lacks a required image

entry.name: stale_frame
entry.summary: frame id unknown or already retired

entry.name: invalid_serial
entry.summary: ack_configure with an unsent or consumed serial

entry.name: wrong_surface
entry.summary: submitted slot was created by another surface

entry.name: already_submitted
entry.summary: submitted slot is awaiting release

entry.name: duplicate_frame
entry.summary: second submission for the same frame id

entry.name: size_mismatch
entry.summary: colour and depth extents differ for a view

entry.name: foreign_object
entry.summary: argument object belongs to another shell domain

enum.name: clipping_mode
enum.description:
How the compositor treats fragments outside the acknowledged bounds. Bounds are half-extents (hw, hh, hd) from the surface origin along its local axes; the front face is the z = +hd face, whose outward normal is +z and faces the viewer.
In cuboid mode a fragment is visible only if |x| <= hw, |y| <= hh and |z| <= hd in model coordinates, boundaries included.
In portal mode a fragment is visible only if z <= hd and, for the view being composed, the fragment lies inside the open frustum whose apex is the view's position (transformed into the surface's model space) and whose edges pass through the four corners of the front face rectangle (|x| <= hw, |y| <= hh, z = hd), boundaries included. Content behind the front face is thereby revealed only through the front face, per view.

entry.name: cuboid
entry.summary: clip to the bounding box

entry.name: portal
entry.summary: clip to the per-view portal frustum

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the role object. The surface is unmapped, pending feedback objects for it receive discarded, and its frame slots become inert: their requests will be ignored except the destroy request, no released events will be sent, and any outstanding compositor access to their images completes internally, after which attached buffers are released and pending release points signalled. The XR role remains assigned to the wl_surface.

request.name: set_clipping_mode
request.description: Set the clipping mode. The mode is latched state: it is captured by the next submit request and applies to that submission and subsequent ones.

request.name: ack_configure
request.description:
Acknowledge a configure event, consuming its serial. Acknowledging a serial the compositor never sent, or one already consumed, raises the invalid_serial error. Acknowledging a serial implicitly consumes all earlier unacknowledged serials of this surface. The acknowledged bounds become the surface's clipping bounds for subsequent submissions.
A client may submit while a newer configure remains unacknowledged; the compositor then clips against the most recently acknowledged bounds.

request.name: create_slot
request.description: Create a frame slot owned by this surface: a reusable container for the per-view colour and depth images of one submission. Clients typically create two or three slots and cycle them as the compositor releases them. Slots are usable only with their creating surface; submitting them elsewhere raises wrong_surface there.

request.name: submit
request.description:
Atomically submit the slot's images as this surface's content for the frame with the given id (combined from frame_hi and frame_lo as described in the protocol preamble).
Requirements, each with its protocol error: the slot must have been created by this surface (wrong_surface); the slot must not be awaiting release (already_submitted); at least one configure must have been acknowledged (unconfigured); the frame id must be announced and not retired (stale_frame); this surface must not have already submitted for this frame id (duplicate_frame); the slot must contain a colour and a depth image for every view in the active view set (incomplete_slot); and for each view the colour and depth extents must be equal (size_mismatch).
The images, their sync points, the depth metadata, the latched clipping mode, and the frame id form one atomic unit. The slot enters the submitted state until its released event.
A submission that arrives after the compositor's composition cutoff for the named frame is not an error: it is discarded — its feedback objects receive discarded, the slot is released without its images being sampled, and the compositor composes a placeholder within the surface's bounds for that frame. The compositor never re-presents previously submitted images for a newer frame.

arg.name: frame_hi
arg.summary: upper 32 bits of the frame id

arg.name: frame_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of the frame id

request.name: clear
request.description: Unmap the surface: the compositor stops composing it after the current frame. Pending feedback objects receive discarded. Slots, their attachments, and acknowledged bounds are unaffected; the next valid submit maps the surface again without a new configure cycle.

event.name: configure
event.description: Suggest a bounding volume, as half-extents in metres from the surface origin along its local axes. The configured state should not be applied immediately: the client acknowledges the serial with ack_configure and renders within the new bounds from its next submission on.

arg.name: half_width
arg.summary: half extent in metres, local x

arg.name: half_height
arg.summary: half extent in metres, local y

arg.name: half_depth
arg.summary: half extent in metres, local z

interface.name: zxr_frame_slot_v2
interface.description:
A reusable container holding, per view, one colour image, one depth image, their explicit-sync timeline points, and the depth encoding metadata. Attachments accumulate in the slot and become surface content only through zxr_surface_v2.submit.
A slot is either idle or submitted. All mutating requests (attach, set_acquire_point, set_release_point, set_depth_range) raise the busy error while the slot is submitted. The slot returns to idle when the released event is sent.
Colour images are sampled opaque: any alpha channel is ignored. Colour values are interpreted per the buffer's format; the full buffer is the image. Depth images carry window-space depth — clip z over w as produced by the snapshot's projection matrix, mapped to the stored range as declared by set_depth_range.

entry.name: unknown_view
entry.summary: view does not belong to this shell domain

entry.name: busy
entry.summary: mutating request while the slot is submitted

entry.name: invalid_format
entry.summary: depth buffer format was not advertised

entry.name: invalid_metadata
entry.summary: depth metadata values out of range

entry.name: missing_sync
entry.summary: dmabuf image submitted without acquire and release points

entry.name: unsupported_sync
entry.summary: sync point set on a non-dmabuf image

entry.name: colour
entry.summary: colour image

entry.name: depth
entry.summary: depth image

entry.name: reversed
entry.summary: stored depth decreases with distance

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the slot. Attached wl_buffers are not affected and remain valid. If the slot is submitted, outstanding compositor access to its images completes internally: buffers are released and pending release points signalled when that access ends; the released event is not sent.

request.name: attach
request.description:
Attach a wl_buffer as the image of the given type for the given view, replacing any previous attachment of that pair; a null buffer removes the attachment, together with its sync points and, for depth, its metadata. If the attached wl_buffer is destroyed while the slot is idle, the attachment is removed likewise.
Depth buffers must use a format advertised through zxr_shell_v2.depth_format; otherwise the invalid_format error is raised. A view object announced by a different shell domain raises the unknown_view error.

request.name: set_acquire_point

description.summary: set the acquire timeline point for one image

request.description:
Set the timeline point that must be signalled before the compositor may sample from the image attached for the given (view, type) pair. Setting a point replaces any previous acquire point for the pair. Points are retained across submissions until replaced or the attachment is removed.
Acquire and release points are required for every dmabuf image; a submission with a dmabuf image lacking either raises the missing_sync error on this object. Setting a point for a non-dmabuf image raises the unsupported_sync error. While any image of a submission carries timeline points, the delivery of wl_buffer.release events for the slot's buffers becomes undefined.

request.name: set_release_point

description.summary: set the release timeline point for one image

request.description:
Set the timeline point that will be signalled by the compositor when it has finished all access to the image attached for the given (view, type) pair for the submission the point accompanies. Setting a point replaces any previous release point for the pair; the point is consumed by the next submit and must be set again before the following one.
Release points of different submissions may signal out of submission order; clients must use a distinct point, and should use a distinct timeline, per in-flight submission of the same buffer to avoid premature-release hazards. The same errors as set_acquire_point apply.

request.name: set_depth_range

description.summary: set the depth encoding for one view

request.description:
Define how stored depth values for the given view map to metric distance. All four scalar arguments are IEEE 754 binary32 values transported as their 32-bit patterns.
A stored value s in [min_depth, max_depth] corresponds to window depth w = (s - min_depth) / (max_depth - min_depth), or w = (max_depth - s) / (max_depth - min_depth) if the reversed flag is set. Window depth w corresponds to the view-space distance d with 1/d = (1/near) + w * ((1/far) - (1/near)). Stored values outside [min_depth, max_depth] are clamped to it.
Requirements, all raising invalid_metadata: min_depth and max_depth in [0, 1] with min_depth strictly less than max_depth; near strictly positive and strictly less than far; all four values finite. This state is consumed together with the attachments it describes at the next submit and is retained until replaced or its depth attachment is removed.

arg.name: near
arg.summary: near distance in metres, binary32 bits

arg.name: far
arg.summary: far distance in metres, binary32 bits

event.name: released

description.summary: the compositor is done with the submission

event.description: Sent when the compositor has finished all sampling from the slot's images for its single outstanding submission; the slot returns to idle. Release points accompanying that submission are signalled no later than this event. For shm images without timeline points, wl_buffer.release is sent no later than this event.

interface.name: zxr_frame_timing_v2
interface.description:
Delivers, once per compositor frame, the atomic snapshot a client needs to render that frame, and announces frame retirement.
The snapshot grammar is fixed: one frame event; then exactly one view_state event for every view in the active view set; then exactly one transform event for every surface of this domain holding the XR role, mapped or not; then one done event carrying the same frame id. Snapshots never nest or interleave. A client may submit against any announced, unretired frame at any time, including while a later snapshot is being delivered.
Timestamps are in the domain clock (zxr_shell_v2.clock), as seconds combined from tv_sec_hi and tv_sec_lo plus tv_nsec nanoseconds; tv_nsec must be in [0, 999999999].

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the timing object. Pending feedback objects are not affected. A new timing object may then be created; frame ids continue from the shell domain's sequence.

request.name: feedback

description.summary: request feedback for the next submission

request.description: Request presentation feedback for the given surface's next submit request. All feedback objects created before that submit are associated with the same submission, each delivering exactly one presented or discarded event, after which the compositor destroys the object. If the surface is destroyed, cleared, or its role object destroyed before feedback resolves, discarded is sent. A surface from another shell domain raises zxr_surface_v2.foreign_object.

event.name: frame
event.description: Opens the snapshot of one frame. The display time is the predicted time the frame's light reaches the user's eyes. The cutoff is the duration before the display time by which submissions for this frame must arrive to be composed; later submissions are discarded as described in zxr_surface_v2.submit. The period is the compositor's current frame period.

arg.name: frame_hi
arg.summary: upper 32 bits of the frame id

arg.name: frame_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of the frame id

arg.name: tv_sec_hi
arg.summary: upper 32 bits of the display time seconds

arg.name: tv_sec_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of the display time seconds

arg.name: cutoff_ns
arg.summary: submission cutoff before display time, nanoseconds

event.name: view_state

description.summary: per-view matrices for the open snapshot

event.description: The view and projection matrices of one active view, valid exactly for the frame of the open snapshot. Clients must render with the matrices of the frame they submit against; matrices from other frames produce misaligned composition.

event.name: transform

description.summary: a surface's world transform for the open snapshot

event.description: The model-to-local-space transform of one XR surface for the frame of the open snapshot. The client renders in its model space; the compositor composes using this transform, so a client must not bake it into its rendering.

event.name: done
event.description: Closes the snapshot opened by the frame event with the same frame id. This allows the matrices, transforms, and timing of a frame to be seen as atomic, even if they happen via multiple events.

arg.name: frame_hi
arg.summary: upper 32 bits of the frame id

arg.name: frame_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of the frame id

event.name: retired

description.summary: a frame id is no longer submittable

event.description: The frame with the given id has been presented, discarded, or superseded and can no longer be submitted against; submissions naming it raise zxr_surface_v2.stale_frame. Every announced frame is eventually retired, and retirement is sent in frame order.

arg.name: frame_hi
arg.summary: upper 32 bits of the frame id

arg.name: frame_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of the frame id

interface.name: zxr_frame_feedback_v2
interface.description: Delivers the outcome of one submission. Exactly one of presented or discarded is sent, after which the compositor destroys the object.

event.name: presented
event.description: The submission was composed into the frame with the given id and reached the display at the given time, in the domain clock. tv_nsec must be in [0, 999999999].

arg.name: frame_hi
arg.summary: upper 32 bits of the frame id

arg.name: frame_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of the frame id

arg.name: tv_sec_hi
arg.summary: upper 32 bits of the presentation time seconds

arg.name: tv_sec_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of the presentation time seconds

event.name: discarded
event.description: The submission's content was never displayed: it missed its frame's cutoff, was superseded, or its surface was cleared or destroyed before presentation.

interface.name: zxr_ray_v2
interface.description:
A pointing ray, following the wl_pointer model: focus is conveyed by enter and leave, motion is delivered in the focused surface's model space, and logically grouped events are terminated by a frame event.
Ray origins and directions are arrays of 3 IEEE 754 binary32 values in native endianness, in the focused surface's model space, in metres; directions are unit length. Timestamps are milliseconds in the domain clock.
If the focused surface's role object or wl_surface is destroyed, focus ends without a leave event; the next enter announces the new focus. If the seat's ray device disappears, this object stops sending events until a device returns.

entry.name: released
entry.summary: button released

entry.name: pressed
entry.summary: button pressed

entry.name: vertical_scroll
entry.summary: vertical scroll

entry.name: horizontal_scroll
entry.summary: horizontal scroll

entry.name: wheel
entry.summary: a physical wheel rotation

entry.name: finger
entry.summary: finger on a touch surface

entry.name: continuous
entry.summary: continuous coordinate space

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the ray object. The seat object and any current focus are not affected.

event.name: enter
event.description: The ray entered the surface's acknowledged bounds and the surface gains ray focus.

arg.name: direction
arg.summary: 3 binary32 values, native endianness, unit length

event.name: leave
event.description: Ray focus left the surface. The leave event is sent before the enter event for any new focus.

event.name: motion
event.description: The ray moved within the focused surface.

arg.name: direction
arg.summary: 3 binary32 values, native endianness, unit length

event.name: button
event.description: A button on the ray's device changed state. The button code is a linux/input-event-codes.h code.

event.name: axis
event.description: Scroll motion on the given axis, as a length in the focused surface's model space.

event.name: axis_source

description.summary: source of the current axis motion

event.description: The source of the axis motion of this event group. Sent at most once per frame group, before the axis events it describes.

event.name: axis_stop
event.description: The motion on the given axis stopped; useful for kinetic scrolling.

event.name: axis_value120
event.description: Discrete high-resolution scroll on the given axis, in fractions of 120 forming one logical scroll step, following the wl_pointer value120 model.

event.name: frame

description.summary: end of a logical event group

event.description: Groups the preceding events into one logical hardware event.

interface.name: zxr_pointer_6dof_v2

description.summary: six degree of freedom pointer device

interface.description: A tracked pointer with position and orientation, following the same focus, frame, and destruction model as zxr_ray_v2. Positions are arrays of 3 IEEE 754 binary32 values in native endianness, in the focused surface's model space, in metres; orientations are arrays of 4 binary32 values forming a unit quaternion per the protocol preamble's convention. Timestamps are milliseconds in the domain clock.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the pointer object. The seat object and any current focus are not affected.

event.name: enter
event.description: The pointer entered the surface's acknowledged bounds and the surface gains pointer focus.

arg.name: orientation
arg.summary: 4 binary32 values, unit quaternion, x y z w

event.name: leave
event.description: Pointer focus left the surface. The leave event is sent before the enter event for any new focus.

event.name: motion
event.description: The pointer moved within the focused surface.

arg.name: orientation
arg.summary: 4 binary32 values, unit quaternion, x y z w

event.name: button
event.description: A button on the pointer's device changed state. The button code is a linux/input-event-codes.h code.

event.name: frame

description.summary: end of a logical event group

event.description: Groups the preceding events into one logical hardware event.
